Options.tools whitelist, allowed_tools, disallowed_tools at session start; mid-session via set_permission_mode, toggle_mcp_server, or PreToolUse deny. Per-turn dynamic filter is not first-class.
Same triad as Python SDK plus toolAliases, AgentDefinition.tools per sub-agent, skills filter, and Query.setMcpServers(servers) for mid-session replace. Per-turn filter requires setMcpServers.
Agent(tools=[...]) fixed at construction. No prepareStep / activeTools. Only mid-run dynamism is BaseTool.max_usage_count cap. MCP tool_filter is connection-level.
ChatModelAgentMiddleware.BeforeAgent gets mutable runCtx.Tools. Per-turn filtering via WrapModel + model.WithTools (toolsearch middleware). Comprehensive.
ai.WithTools(...) per Generate call; engineer branches by tenantID before the call. No per-turn activeTools. Middleware.Tools can only add, not remove.
Three mechanisms: bind_tools upstream, dynamic model selection callable per turn with bound tools, wrap_tool_call short-circuit. Per-turn filter is first-class via dynamic model.
FunctionAgent(tool_retriever=ObjectRetriever) is called each turn with current user_msg_str — true per-turn dynamic filtering. Also static tools list at construction.

Three layers: dynamic tools = DynamicArgument receiving requestContext; activeTools whitelist per call; prepareStep returning { activeTools } per step; toolCallStep rejects non-active tools. First-class per-turn filtering.

agent.run(messages, options={tools:[...]}) override per call; ContextProvider can contribute tools; FilteringSkillsSource for skills. No per-turn activeTools. tool_choice/allowed_tools where provider supports.
Tool.is_enabled accepts bool or (RunContextWrapper, AgentBase) -> bool callable, evaluated in Agent.get_all_tools per-turn. First-class per-turn filter. Handoffs also support is_enabled.
Per-tool isEnabled: ({ runContext, agent }) => boolean | Promise<boolean> evaluated in Agent.getAllTools each turn. Handoffs support it too. First-class.

Per-step PrepareTools capability returning filtered list[ToolDefinition]; .filtered()/.prepared()/.renamed() wrappers on any AbstractToolset; @agent.toolset decorator builds toolsets from RunContext. Per-run toolsets= kwarg.

No activeTools / allowedTools / prepareStep. Workaround is to build a fresh Agent via AgentBuilder per request with only the tools you want. Mutating shared ToolServerHandle affects all concurrent users.

Agent(tools=[...]) at construction; per-turn requires mutating agent.tool_registry.registry / dynamic_tools between turns or using BeforeToolCallEvent.selected_tool = None to veto. Not exposed as per-turn filter.
ToolRegistry read once per model call; no per-turn prepareStep. Workarounds: per-tenant Agent, mutate registry between cycles, BeforeToolCallEvent cancel. Not first-class.
Three layers: activeTools at construction, prepareStep returning {activeTools} per step (used by filterActiveTools), prepareCall returning {tools} per call. First-class per-step filtering.
Session has AppName, UserID, ID and State map. No Session.TenantID first-class field. Convention is AppName==tenant or app:tenant_id in state.

AgentSession has user_id/agent_id/team_id/workflow_id but no tenant_id column. Stuff in session.metadata or dependencies. AgentOS JWT scopes recognize agent-os:<os-id>:<resource>:<id> for HTTP-layer tenant separation.
Neither Task nor Context nor AgentConfig carries a tenant field. Per-tenant requires BYO at the host layer.

SessionKey.project_key is the documented multi-tenant primitive for the session store. Docstring: 'Multi-tenant deployments should set this to a tenant ID or project name.' Scopes session storage only, not toolset/skills.
Same as Python: SessionKey.projectKey explicitly documented for multi-tenant deployments. No tenantId on Options or SDKSessionInfo. Tenant modeled via cwd + projectKey + env.
No tenant_id anywhere. Grep finds only DEFAULT_TENANT for ChromaDB. Tenant only in Crew.config / execution_context / OTel baggage. Not architected for multi-tenant in-process serving.
No first-class tenant field on session. WithSessionValues(map[string]any{'tenantId': ...}) is the convention; GetSessionValue reads it back. Untyped.
No Tenant field on Session. Add tenant to your typed state S struct and key session store by tenant:userId:sessionId. Pure convention.

No Session.tenant_id column. Practice: stamp metadata['owner'] = tenant_id on thread creation via @auth.on.threads.create (LangGraph Server) AND store tenant_id in Runtime.context. @auth.on.* on Platform provides FilterType for SQL filters.
No first-class tenant_id. Stuff in ctx.store (generic KV) or Memory.session_id (single string encoding tenant:user:conversation).

Tenant identity not a single top-level field, but reserved RequestContext keys (resourceId, threadId, authToken) are first-class and explicitly server-preserved for security. RBAC + FGA consume requestContext for permission checks.
session.state['tenant_id'] or AgentSessionStateBag['tenant_id']. Not first-class. No HTTP-layer policy.
Session.session_id: str is the only identity. Conventions: encode 'acme:user-123:conv-abc' or carry in TContext. trace_metadata for OTel tagging.
Session interface has only sessionId: string. Encode tenant in id or via custom Session impl scoping by tenant out-of-band.
No first-class field. Idiomatic pattern: typed deps dataclass with tenant_id + metadata={'tenant_id': ...} for OTel/Logfire tagging. Both accessible from every hook and tool.
Tenants encoded in conversation_id (e.g. 'tenant=acme;user=u-123;thread=42') and in tool closures. Not first-class.
Session/SessionAgent/SessionMessage carry no tenant column. Encode tenancy in session_id (e.g. 'acme:user-123:thread-abc') and/or agent.state.
SnapshotLocation has sessionId/scope/scopeId — none tenant. Encode into sessionId or invocationState. Not first-class.
There is no session in v7-canary, so no session-level tenant. Convention is runtimeContext.tenantId only; persistence is host's job.
context.Context carries OAuth tokens you put there; ctx.UserID()/AppName() exposed. No first-class principal/claims type. authPreprocessor is for tool-auth flows, not request-time identity.
Auth principal (JWT sub) propagated to user_id on RunContext by AgentOS router. RemoteAgent calls forward JWT via auth_token kwarg. Tools read run_context.user_id.

note: 0 — caller identity does not reach tool
details: No mechanism. Capture identity as a tool struct field at construction time. Per-request identity propagation requires per-request agent build.
No SDK primitive automatically threads caller's JWT to every tool. Closure capture into hook/tool callbacks is the standard pattern.

Caller's identity does not flow into tool calls automatically. SDK-MCP tools can pull identity from request context (AsyncLocalStorage); built-in CLI tools run under subprocess identity. PreToolUse.updatedInput for per-call signing tokens.
Caller's identity does not propagate. crew_context OTel baggage carries crew.id/key only. Tools authenticated per-instance, not per-request.
No built-in identity propagation. Engineer puts identity on context.Context and reads inside tool. No automatic STS/impersonation.

ContextProvider reads request.Headers (Authorization, etc.) and populates ActionContext. Tools read core.FromContext(ctx) to access. Firebase plugin ships auth helper. Each tool decides what to enforce.

runtime.context carries caller's identity into every tool. Tools execute with whatever DB credentials engineer wires into runtime.context (e.g. tenant-scoped DB connection). LangGraph Server @auth.on adds HTTP-layer auth.
Auth identity is whatever you stash in ctx.store and read inside the tool. No built-in propagation from an outer HTTP handler.

Reserved key MASTRA_AUTH_TOKEN_KEY is the canonical channel for forwarding caller's auth token into tool execution. Tools read ctx.requestContext.get(MASTRA_AUTH_TOKEN_KEY); editor uses this to forward auth to MCP servers.
Caller identity is not automatic. Inject via function_invocation_kwargs (Python) or AgentRunOptions.AdditionalProperties (.NET). ToolApprovalAgent handles approval, not identity propagation.
TContext naturally carries user OAuth tokens, tenant scoping rules, RLS predicates. ToolContext exposes tool_call_id/agent for correlation. Documented pattern with Okta examples.
Whatever you put in runContext.context is automatically reachable from every tool, hook, guardrail, handoff. SDK does not perform HTTP-auth check at tool boundary; you do it inside execute.
ctx.deps flows to every tool. Host code that constructs deps (from HTTP request) is the auth termination point. Typed dataclass so OAuth tokens are first-class.
No principal, no auth_token, no per-call identity. Tools execute with whatever permissions were baked into their call body.
Whatever you stash in invocation_state (and/or agent.state) is forwarded to every tool via invocation_state.update. No first-class JWT/OAuth object — BYO.
Caller's identity propagates via invocationState only. No built-in auth principal type; tools execute under host process credentials and pass per-call auth via invocationState.userId/.scopes/.jwt.
Caller identity reaches tool only if you put it there. runtimeContext + toolsContext are the channels. No magic — pure BYO.
No publish-time tenant tag. FilterToolset/Predicate is the only mechanism; sub-agents are static SubAgents list. Skills: wrap sources by tenant (hand-rolled MergedSource).
Per-Agent skills, no tenant scoping at loader. Members (Team) and tools support callable factories per request. No first-class register-for-tenant-X.
Framework-level scoping not provided. Implement at host's registration layer (per-tenant AgentBuilder factory).

Scoping mechanism is the filesystem: skills, sub-agents, slash commands, MCP config, CLAUDE.md from setting_sources (user/project/local). Per-tenant requires per-tenant filesystem tree + cwd + CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR env.
Same as Python: skills/agents/commands all filesystem-based under cwd. Programmatic Options.agents for sub-agents. Cannot register a resource as 'tenant X only' via API call.
Skills scoped by filesystem path at agent construction; tools/sub-agents scoped by membership. No global/tenant/user hierarchy at registration. AMP Agent Repositories are org-wide.
No publish-time scopes. Build a custom skill.Backend returning different FrontMatter lists per ctx tenant. Pure runtime.
Tools/prompts/retrievers/evaluators registered in a single global Registry per Genkit instance. No register-with-scope. Scoping is your job at Generate-call time.

BaseStore.put((namespace_tuple,), key, value) — namespace tuple naturally supports per-tenant-per-user. @auth.on decorators with FilterType apply SQL filters to threads/runs/assistants/crons/store. Strong on Platform; OSS is namespace only.
Not provided. Pass tenant-scoped tool lists at agent construction or filter in tool_retriever.

Skills, sub-agents, workspaces, memory all support DynamicArgument receiving requestContext — per-request resolution. Versions per-call sub-agent version pinning via MASTRA_VERSIONS_KEY. No built-in org/channel/user hierarchy — encode via FGA rules.
Tools/skills/sub-agents filtered at registration via FilteringSkillsSource / AggregatingSkillsSource. No publish-time tenant tag — compose a different SkillsProvider per tenant.
Per-agent at construction; per-call via is_enabled callables. No registry concept — roll your own dict-of-agent-per-tenant for registry-layer scoping.
No registration-time scope. Filtering is runtime-only via isEnabled / handoff isEnabled / callModelInputFilter.
Toolsets/capabilities scoped per-run via run kwargs. Dynamic capabilities resolve at run time from RunContext (load_skill(ctx.deps.user_id, ctx.deps.tenant_id)). Not first-class hierarchy.
No global/tenant/user scopes at registration. Everything registered on Agent or ToolServerHandle.
tool_registry is a flat global dict; no registration-time scoping. Enforce at hook layer (BeforeToolCallEvent inspects invocation_state['tenant_id'] and blocks tools not in allowlist).
Tools, hooks, plugins register globally on an Agent instance. Only Snapshot.scope is 'agent' | 'multiAgent'. Per-tenant scope is host's job.

Per-tool contextSchema declares expected context; validateToolContext rejects mismatches at runtime. Per-call RUNTIME_CONTEXT typing. No global/tenant scope — template the agent or filter activeTools by tenant.
No MaxTokens-per-tenant, no USD cap, no rate-limit middleware. MaxConcurrentRuns is global to a trigger. Token counts on Event.UsageMetadata for BYO rollup.
tool_call_limit per agent (count cap, not budget). Metrics.cost reported in USD post-hoc but not enforced. Per-tenant enforcement is BYO.
Only a turn cap (default 10). No USD budget, no per-tenant cost tracking. Build on top of Usage from StreamChunk.

Real per-run USD budget cap via max_budget_usd → --max-budget-usd. On overrun the run ends with error_max_budget_usd. Post-call check (cost may exceed by one call). No per-tenant aggregation primitive — BYO sum total_cost_usd.

Options.maxBudgetUsd: USD ceiling enforced server-side. Plus maxTurns and taskBudget.total (alpha token budget visible to model). Only first-party USD cost cap in the benchmark. Per-tenant aggregation is BYO.
Agent.max_rpm / Crew.max_rpm enforce RPM via RPMController — process-local, not per-tenant. UsageMetrics tracks tokens; no cost_usd. completion_cost field exists but no code path populates it.
No USD budget enforcement, no per-tenant token ceiling. Read token counts off ResponseMeta.Usage in callbacks.Handler.OnEnd and enforce yourself.
No USD budget. Only MaxTurns (turn count). Token usage on resp.Usage; enforce limits yourself (probably WrapGenerate middleware checking Redis counter).
No token-budget cap, no USD-cost cap in OSS. LangGraph Platform has per-deployment rate limits but not per-tenant USD ceilings.
TokenCountingHandler has token_budget that raises ValueError if exceeded — per handler instance, counts tokens (not USD). No USD budget cap.

CostGuardProcessor fires tripwire when cost exceeds threshold but relies on caller-provided pricing (CostContext.estimatedCost). stopWhen supports maxSteps and tokenLimit. No native USD ceiling; combine for per-tenant cap.
Tokens observable via OTel histograms and UsageDetails, but no built-in USD-cap or per-tenant ceiling.
Usage reports tokens (input/output/total/cached/reasoning) and request counts. No dollar-cost field, no per-tenant budget cap, no 'stop if usage > $X'. Enforce in on_llm_end hook or post-hoc.
SDK surfaces token usage (RunContext.usage) but does not enforce caps. Enforce via agent_tool_start listener that throws or custom Model wrapper that pre-checks usage.
UsageLimits caps per-run tokens/requests/tool calls (request_limit=50 default). No USD cap in-tree; Pydantic AI Gateway adds project/user/key-level daily/weekly/monthly USD caps. Per-tenant via hook.
Only max_turns (turn cap) and max_tokens (per-completion cap). No USD budget, no per-tenant rate limit.
EventLoopMetrics.update_usage tracks tokens at agent-instance level. Aggregate per-tenant and enforce in hooks. BYO.
accumulatedUsage (input/output tokens) on AgentMetrics, no USD cost computation, no enforcement. Enforce via BeforeModelCallEvent checking projectedInputTokens or polling metrics from host.
stopWhen accepts step-count and tool-name stop conditions, but no USD-cost or token-count budget cap in the SDK. AI Gateway's spend report is observational, not enforcing.
Eval is Python-only in ADK; the Go server exposes ListEvalSets/ListEvalResults routes but they return HTTP 501 via controllers.Unimplemented. No dataset format, runner, or harness ships in adk-go.

Agno ships first-party AccuracyEval / PerformanceEval / ReliabilityEval / AgentAsJudge classes in libs/agno/agno/eval/, with results persisted to the agno_evals table via db.create_eval_run. Not as dataset-centric as pydantic-evals (no separate Dataset/Case file format), but the harness is built in and usable for regression.

No Dataset, no Evaluator, no EvalRun ship in AutoAgents; the report flags 'Not provided — BYO'. A `parallel.rs` evaluator exists in autoagents-llm but it is for internal parallelism, not regression eval.
Report marks this red: no golden-dataset format, no regression harness ships with the Python SDK. You build it yourself around query().
No golden-dataset format and no regression harness; only a SessionStore conformance suite exists (adapter test, not agent regression). Users build eval harnesses themselves over query().

`crewai test [-n N]` runs the crew N times and CrewEvaluator scores task outputs via an LLM, printing a table. However there is no dataset format: you re-run with whatever inputs are in the script (or via kickoff_for_each), so regression suite semantics are partial.
